To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the hypothalamus is the central regulator of body weight, that the key components of its regulatory network are neuropeptide Y, melanocortin-4 receptors, pro-opiomelanocortin, and agouti-related protein, that these molecules are expressed in distinct populations of neurons, and that they interact with one another to produce coordinated control of food intake, energy expenditure, and body weight.
The hypothalamus is the primary brain region that controls food intake and body-weight homeostasis.
the hypothalamic arcuate nucleus is a key site at which signals from peripheral energy stores are integrated to regulate feeding and body weight.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the neural control of food intake, energy expenditure, body weight and body fat stores.
how the brain regulates energy homeostasis.
the mechanisms by which the body regulates food intake and body fat stores.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the central nervous system is the master regulator of energy balance, and that its function is impaired in obesity.
the central nervous system is a complex system of interacting neuronal networks, which are involved in the control of food intake, energy expenditure, and body weight.
obesity is a complex disease with a multifactorial etiology.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are interested in understanding the mechanisms that control feeding behaviour and energy homeostasis.
we are trying to understand the molecular, cellular, and behavioural mechanisms of body weight regulation.
we are trying to understand how the brain controls food intake and bodyweight and how this control can go wrong to cause obesity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the brain can sense changes in energy stores and respond with adjustments in feeding behaviour.
the central control of body weight is not a simple matter of sensing body fat stores and adjusting food intake to maintain a setpoint.
the brain is the master controller of body weight, and that it is possible to change the brain's set point and thereby change the weight set point of the body.
